elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.6 retains the proviso, now limited to us: "PB may assign, sublicense or transfer this Agreement and all of its rights and obligations hereunder, in their entirety, to any of its Affiliates" — no SFJ consent required.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same proviso: "or to a successor in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise" — covers merger, stock sale and substantially-all-assets transfers without consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The opening prohibition ("Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto ... neither Party will sell, transfer, assign ...") now has its only carve-out narrowed from "either Party" to "PB", so every SFJ assignment, including to affiliates or successors, requires PB's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted qualifier "Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto, not to be unreasonably withheld" attaches the reasonableness standard to the consent SFJ must obtain from PB (and symmetrically).

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Final paragraph, with the Program Transfer sunset sentence deleted and "prior to the date of Program Transfer" replaced by "at any time": SFJ shall not transfer the Agreement to "an entity whose primary business is the development or commercialization of pharmaceutical or biotechnology products at any time". The only relief is PB's consent "withheld in PB's sole discretion", i.e. a Customer-controlled absolute veto, and the "Notwithstanding any of the foregoing" opener keeps it clear of the new reasonableness standard.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2.6 (heading de-titled to "Change of Control of PB") states "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB", and the sole-discretion termination right plus the 150% Development Costs payment machinery and its post-termination consequences (p0766) are deleted.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor/affiliate carve-out was deliberately narrowed to "PB"; SFJ may assign to a successor only with PB's prior written consent, so the mutual successor right the fallback requires does not exist in the rendered text.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.6 contains no notice obligation for a consent-free successor transfer; the only notice duty in the redline is PB's Change of Control notice retained in 14.2.6, which is not an assignment-notice mechanic.

"Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto ... neither Party will sell, transfer, assign, pledge or otherwise dispose of ... this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder".

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted "not to be unreasonably withheld" qualifies the mutual consent requirement in the opening sentence of 15.6.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all six preferred elements are met in operative language (PB-only affiliate/successor carve-out, mutual consent gate now binding SFJ, reasonableness standard, perpetual competitor bar, and an express "no right to terminate" on PB Change of Control).

Fallback level is not complete (mutual successor right and written-notice mechanic are absent), but that is immaterial because the drafter targeted the preferred level, and the rationale correctly explains that using the fallback would surrender our existing consent-free affiliate carve-out.

Minimality defect: the second sentence added to 14.2.6, "This Agreement shall continue in full force and effect following a Change of Control of PB.", is declaratory boilerplate that duplicates the operative effect of the immediately preceding "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB." No selected element requires it. Delete that sentence; the no-termination sentence alone carries the element.

Otherwise the edits are tightly scoped: "either Party" narrowed to "PB", the reasonableness qualifier inserted, "prior to the date of Program Transfer" changed to "at any time" with its avoidance-of-doubt sunset removed, and the 14.2.6 termination right deleted. Deleting the 150% Development Costs payment and the p0766 consequences paragraph is proper rather than over-reach, since both were contingent solely on a termination under 14.2.6 that no longer exists; retaining them would have left dangling "such termination" references.

Intent preserved: PB's Change of Control notice duty, PB's Buy-Out Option (6.7.2), and SFJ's limited-partner/liquidating-trust right to assign receipt of Approval Payments are untouched, and the "Notwithstanding any of the foregoing" opener keeps PB's sole-discretion competitor veto from conflicting with the new reasonableness standard. One drafting check before sending: confirm no other provision (e.g. effects-of-termination or Article 6 adjustment provisions) cross-references "Section 14.2.6" as a termination event, so the deletion leaves no dangling cross-reference.
